item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
So we have SCP-553; the slicing, stone butterflies. SCP-1641; the exploding, metal butterflies. And of course, SCP-408; the sentient, camouflaging butterflies.

Now I'm just going to sit back and wait for the "War of the Butterflies" to be written!

There are also a few other butterfly related scips, but those are the main three that come to mind. (SCP-820 also comes to mind, but that's a swarm of locust, not butterflies.)

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I'd have to agree with Bold up there. What was there was good, but it wasn't really enough to grasp any interest. Also, isn't it kinda bad to be writing one of these more "classic" style tales that might confuse the hell out of a lot of newbies (yo) who would see this and not understand that this isn't the main fare of the website anymore?

The writing itself is good, but it just sends a bad message in my brain.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
While I like the premise (Zyn stopping an army of robots with butterflies. That's kinda cool.) the tone of the writing is really dry and uninspired. Gears's one-liner is weak, and I'd really like to see more detail and greater depth to the action. Right now it feels more like a plot synopsis of a longer tale than a tale unto itself.

-1
